2025 Mathematics, Rebuilt Month by Month

Revised questions, precise statements, proofs, examples and reproducible checks, organized by source month.

This volume rebuilds mathematics recovered from conversations dated in 2025, month by month. Each developed treatment contains a newly revised question, definitions and hypotheses, a precise result, a proof or derivation, a worked example, limits and a further mathematical problem. Related source formulas may be grouped or developed separately where they ask distinct questions.

All twelve months have dated mathematical evidence. Recovery is bounded and fragmentary, rather than an exhaustive export of every historical message. Dates are retained in UTC when available. U identifies a retrieved user-attributed topic or passage; A identifies assistant-only evidence; T identifies a topic or secondary-source fragment. U does not by itself establish that an original prompt was recovered verbatim.

Historical evidence and the new mathematics are separate. The revised questions, proofs and stipulated examples are authored for this volume. Exact source excerpts and receipt locators are retained in the searchable edition and source bundle. Missing original operators, tables, data and proofs are not reconstructed as if their historical bytes were available.

The scope is mathematics. Classical results, new expositions, exact finite certificates, numerical examples and open conjectures are distinguished. Claims about physical devices, model-training performance, or major open problems require their own evidence; the mathematical developments here do not certify such claims. The supplied check programs test their stated finite cases and do not replace written proofs.

Revised question

When does doubling produce6.02dB, and how do coherent amplitudes differ from independent power additions?

The same physical ratio has different numerical logarithmic factors depending on whether one starts with power or amplitude. Coherent addition and independent addition are different hypotheses, with exact phase-dependent formulas.

Definitions and assumptions

For positive powers defineL=10log₁₀(P/P₀). IfP=cA² with fixed positivec, the same level difference is20log₁₀(A/A₀).

Two equal complex amplitudesA andAe^{iφ} sum coherently. Independent zero-mean signals with no cross covariance add their powers instead.

All logarithm arguments must be dimensionless ratios with the same reference convention.

Exact doubling and interference laws

Doubling amplitude at fixed conversionc quadruples power and adds20log₁₀2≈6.02060dB. Doubling power adds10log₁₀2≈3.01030dB. Equal coherent amplitudes giveP_total/P_single=2+2cosφ.

Derivation or proof

The amplitude-to-power law givesP₂/P₁=(A₂/A₁)², so ten times the logarithm of power becomes twenty times the amplitude logarithm. For coherent addition, |A+Ae^{iφ}|²=|A|²(2+e^{iφ}+e^{−iφ})=2|A|²(1+cosφ). Atφ=0 power is four times one signal; atφ=π it is zero. For independent or uncorrelated zero-mean signals, expectation of the cross term vanishes, leaving twice the single-signal power and the3.01dB result. These calculations identify exactly which statistical or phase assumption changes the reported gain.

Worked example

Compare phases zero,π/2 andπ for equal-amplitude inputs.

The power ratios are four,two and zero. The first gives6.02060dB, the second3.01030dB, and exact cancellation has no finite logarithmic level relative to positiveP₀. Rounding6.02 does not convert an amplitude statement into a universal gain for two devices or two noisy sources.

The original identity is preserved with its mathematical domain and operational meaning made explicit.

Scope

Changing impedance or another amplitude-to-power conversion factor changes the simple20log formula. The result does not validate any proposed phonon, curvature or material-protection mechanism.

Further development

For unequal amplitudesA,B, deriveP=A²+B²+2ABcosφ and propagate a bounded phase error through it. The derivative−2ABsinφ shows where a phase-sensitive operating point is locally robust and where it is sensitive. Near destructive interference write φ=π+δ. Then P_total=2A²(1−cosδ)≤A²δ². The inequality 1−cosδ≤δ²/2 gives a global quadratic upper bound on leakage from a phase error, a stronger and more useful robustness statement than merely reporting the zero at perfect cancellation.

Revised question

Which algebraic facts certify a controlled gate, and what quantitative assumption is needed to call a circuit protected?

CNOT is an exact permutation unitary and creates an entangled state from a separable input. A telescoping estimate bounds accumulated implementation error, but unitarity alone does not prove fault tolerance.

Definitions and assumptions

DefineCNOT|a,b⟩=|a,b⊕a⟩ for binary labels. The Hadamard gate sends|0⟩ to(|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2.

For unitary gatesU₁,…,U_m and unitary approximationsV₁,…,V_m assume||V_j−U_j||≤ε_j in operator norm.

Protection is a statement about specified errors, encoding, correction and a performance bound, not merely a name for the intended gate.

Exact entangling gate and circuit error bound

CNOT²=I andCNOT is unitary. CNOT(H⊗I)|00⟩=(|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2, whose one-qubit marginal isI/2. The two circuit products differ by at mostΣ_jε_j.

Derivation or proof

CNOT permutes the four orthonormal basis states and is its own inverse, proving unitarity. Applying it to(|00⟩+|10⟩)/√2 gives the displayed Bell state. Taking a partial trace eliminates the two off-diagonal cross terms and leaves equal populations, so the pure joint state is not a product. For the error bound, subtractV_m⋯V₁−U_m⋯U₁ and insert mixed products one gate at a time. The resulting sum has termsV_m⋯V_{j+1}(V_j−U_j)U_{j−1}⋯U₁. Unitary factors have norm one, so submultiplicativity and the triangle inequality giveΣ ε_j. This is a worst-case coherent-error estimate and requires no stochastic independence.

Worked example

Take ten gates each with norm error at most10⁻³.

The final unitary error is at most10⁻². Acting on any normalized state gives state-vector error at most10⁻²; an expectation of an observable of norm one changes by at most2·10⁻². This bound does not imply a threshold theorem or a percentage of operational coherence.

A correct gate and a protected implementation are separate mathematical claims with a calculable bridge only after errors are specified.

Scope

The calculation supplies no material implementation or hardware error rate. Fault-tolerant thresholds involve coding, locality, noise and repeated recovery assumptions absent from the recovered formulas.

Further development

Choose an explicit encoding and noise channel, verify the Knill–Laflamme conditions and compute a logical error bound after recovery. Compare it with the coherent telescoping bound before claiming protection.

Revised question

Which explicit constructions connect the classical oscillator to prequantization and a quantum ground state?

On the symplectic plane one can write the prequantum connection and verify its curvature directly. The constant-Poisson Moyal product and a normalized Gaussian then give exact, separately checkable quantization statements.

Definitions and assumptions

Use coordinates(q,p),ω=dq∧dp,H=(q²+p²)/2 andħ>0. DefineX_H byι_Xω=dH, givingX_H=p∂q−q∂p.

On the trivial complex line bundle set∇=d−(i/ħ)q dp. The formal Moyal product isf⋆g=f exp[(iħ/2)(←∂q→∂p−←∂p→∂q)]g.

The Schrödinger operator isĤ=−(ħ²/2)d²/dq²+q²/2 on an appropriateL² domain.

Exact curvature and quantization checks

The connection has curvature−iω/ħ. The star commutatorq⋆p−p⋆q=iħ, andH⋆H=H²−ħ²/4. The Gaussianψ₀=(πħ)^−1/4exp(−q²/(2ħ)) is normalized and has energyħ/2.

Derivation or proof

Because the connection one-form is scalar, its wedge square vanishes and∇²=d[−iq dp/ħ]=−i dq∧dp/ħ. Forq,p the bidifferential expansion stops after first derivatives, yieldingqp±iħ/2. ForH⋆H the first Poisson term is zero; the second derivative combination isH_qqH_pp+H_ppH_qq=2, so its coefficient is−ħ²/8 times two. Higher derivatives vanish. Differentiating the Gaussian givesψ₀″=(q²/ħ²−1/ħ)ψ₀, so substitution cancelsq² and leavesħψ₀/2. Its squared norm is one by the elementary Gaussian integral. Formal associativity of the Moyal product follows because the constant-coefficient operators on three tensor factors commute, making both parenthesizations the same exponential of the sum of pair operators.

Worked example

Setħ=1 and compare the classical fixed point with the Gaussian.

The classical point(q,p)=(0,0) hasH=0. The normalized quantum state has energy1/2 and variances〈q²〉=〈p²〉=1/2, givingΔqΔp=1/2. The difference is a quantified statement about a specified representation, not a change in the classical curvature formula.

Each bridge has an explicit map or calculation and can be checked independently.

Scope

Prequantization alone does not choose a polarization or prove the full oscillator spectrum. The formal star product is not automatically a convergent product on every function space.

Further development

Construct the ladder operators, prove their commutator on Schwartz functions and derive all Gaussian–Hermite eigenstates. Then justify completeness and the self-adjoint operator domain rather than relying only on formal algebra. Since H is quadratic, every third derivative vanishes and its Moyal commutator with a polynomial equals iħ times the Poisson bracket exactly. In particular (q⋆H−H⋆q)/(iħ)=p and (p⋆H−H⋆p)/(iħ)=−q, reproducing the classical linear oscillator equations with no higher-order correction.

Revised question

What isH*_{S¹}(R²) for the oscillator rotation action, and why does contractibility not make it ordinary point cohomology?

The plane contracts to its origin equivariantly, so its equivariant cohomology isH*(BS¹)=k[u]. Ordinary plane and free-loop-space cohomology are instead justk. These are different constructions with different retained symmetry data.

Definitions and assumptions

LetS¹ rotateC≅R². The Borel construction isES¹×_{S¹}C, and equivariant cohomology is its ordinary cohomology.

Use characteristic-zero coefficients andu∈H²(BS¹;k), withBS¹≃CP∞. Its cohomology ring isk[u].

The ordinary free-loop spaceLC consists of continuous mapsS¹→C; it does not include the Borel quotient unless explicitly added.

Complete equivariant calculation for the plane

H*_{S¹}(C;k)≅k[u], with one generator in every nonnegative even degree and none in odd degree. H*(C;k)=H*(LC;k)=k in degree zero only.

Derivation or proof

The homotopyr_s(z)=(1−s)z commutes with rotations and ends at the fixed origin. It descends to a deformation retraction ofES¹×_{S¹}C ontoES¹×_{S¹}{0}=BS¹. The standard cell decomposition ofCP∞ has one cell in every even dimension and no odd cells; its ring generatoru has nonzero powers, yieldingk[u]. For the ordinary loop space, contract every loop pointwise byr_s. This is a continuous contraction to the zero loop, giving the ordinary cohomology claim. Thus an exterior factor from the two-dimensional tangent space does not belong automatically to Borel cohomology; such a factor would require a separately specified complex or theory.

Worked example

Compare the first four cohomological degrees.

The equivariant dimensions in degrees0,1,2,3 are1,0,1,0. OrdinaryC andLC have dimensions1,0,0,0. The origin’s stabilizer is the whole circle, which explains the surviving degree-two class in the quotient construction despite the underlying plane being contractible.

The calculation repairs a conflation of loop cohomology, tangent exterior algebra and equivariant cohomology.

Scope

A claimed spectral-sequence degeneration needs its actual fibration or filtered complex and differential bidegrees. No such general degeneration follows merely from the oscillator notation.

Further development

Replace the weight-one rotation byz↦g^m z and compute the equivariant Euler classmu of the normal complex line. Check fixed-point localization only after specifying the coefficient localization and an equivariant integration map. Remove the origin and the rotation action becomes free. The Borel construction of C* is homotopy equivalent to its radial quotient (0,∞), so its equivariant cohomology is k. The restriction map from k[u] therefore kills u. This example shows exactly where a fixed stabilizer contributes additional classes.

Revised question

What algebraic data can actually be extracted from a specified unipotent monodromy before adding a quantum correction?

A two-dimensional unipotent matrix supplies an exact logarithm, a centered weight filtration and a compatible sl₂ representation. This concrete calculation isolates the linear algebra used in degeneration theory from an unprovided quantum enrichment.

Definitions and assumptions

Let V=Qe₁⊕Qe₂ and M=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Its nilpotent logarithm is N=logM=M−I because(M−I)²=0.

A monodromy weight filtration centered at one is increasing, satisfiesN(W_k)⊂W_{k−2}, and makesNʲ:Gr^W_{1+j}→Gr^W_{1−j} an isomorphism for every j≥0.

Explicit monodromy weight calculation

Linear interpolation between successive sample values then stays within2ε ofγ there; choosing a smallerε gives the required strict bound. Compare the unit circle, the constant loopγ≡1 and the triangle joining the cube roots of unity.

The circle and triangle each wind once around zero; the constant loop has winding zero although it returns to its start. Refining equal-angle inscribed polygons of the circle makes the uniform interpolation error tend to zero. The strict distance condition prevents an approximating edge from cutting through zero.

Strings, loops and polygons are now distinguished by precise properties rather than by an assumed progression from closure to a particular shape.

All inclusion maps follow directly from these chain generators. The interval decomposition is therefore explicit rather than merely asserted. Write the finite matrix for the only nontrivial map in low degrees.

Revised question

Can a claimed nonzero flux Jacobiator be distinguished from the identically zero Jacobiator of associative operator commutators?

Associative commutators satisfy Jacobi by cancellation. An explicit octonion triple has a nonzero Jacobiator, furnishing a concrete nonassociative example without identifying it with a physicalR-flux.

For a bilinear multiplication define[a,b]=ab−ba andJ(a,b,c)=[a,[b,c]]+[b,[c,a]]+[c,[a,b]].

Use octonion unitse₁,…,e₇ with squares−1 and oriented Fano triples(123),(145),(176),(246),(257),(347),(365); reversing an ordered pair changes sign.

The associator is(a,b,c)=(ab)c−a(bc). Parentheses cannot be omitted in a nonassociative product.

An exact nonzero Jacobiator

For(a,b,c)=(e₁,e₂,e₄), the associator is2e₇ andJ=−12e₇. In every associative algebra the same commutator formula hasJ=0.

Derivation or proof

In an associative algebra expand the three nested commutators. Each of the six ordered triple products occurs twice with opposite signs, giving zero. In the specified octonion table,e₂e₄=e₆,e₁e₆=−e₇, so[e₁,[e₂,e₄]]=−4e₇. Alsoe₄e₁=−e₅,e₂e₅=e₇, giving the second term−4e₇. Finallye₁e₂=e₃,e₄e₃=−e₇ gives the third−4e₇. Their sum is−12e₇. Separately(e₁e₂)e₄=e₃e₄=e₇, wherease₁(e₂e₄)=e₁e₆=−e₇, giving associator2e₇. This verifies the sign convention rather than appealing to a generic nonassociative slogan. Left multiplication still represents every octonion as a linear map, but it is not a product-preserving representation: L_{e₁}L_{e₂}e₄=−e₇ whereas L_{e₁e₂}e₄=e₇. Commutators of the linear maps satisfy Jacobi, while the octonion commutators need not. This prevents confusing an operator embedding with an associative algebra embedding.

Worked example

Compare this triple with the quaternionic subalgebra spanned by1,e₁,e₂,e₃.

Within that four-dimensional subalgebra multiplication is associative and every commutator Jacobiator vanishes. The chosen triple involvinge₄ leaves that subalgebra and gives the nonzero value above. Thus a large algebra can contain associative sectors without being associative globally.

A nonzero Jacobiator is now attached to a declared multiplication table and a checked triple.

Scope

Ordinary bounded matrices cannot realize this multiplication associatively while preserving all products, since their commutators always satisfy Jacobi. A physicalR-flux interpretation needs a separately defined bracket, observables and consistency rules; it is not derived from the table.

Test alternativity(a,a,b)=(b,a,a)=0 on the full basis and extend by polarization. Then compare the resulting commutator algebra with the Malcev identity, which replaces Lie Jacobi in this setting.

Integratingφ from zero to2π andθ from zero toπ yields2π. IfF=dA for a single smooth globalA, Stokes’ theorem on the closed sphere would force the integral to zero, a contradiction. The state therefore needs at least two phase charts. Multiplyingu bye^{−iφ} gives a southern choice whose potential differs by−dφ, encoding a winding-one transition. This is the local-to-global mechanism behind the integer, not an assumed physical protection law.

Each benefit increases, so capacity is exhausted. Lagrange optimality givesa_i/(1+x_i)=λ on positive coordinates and a_i≤λ on zero coordinates. These conditions yield the formula and are sufficient by concavity. For the example both coordinates are positive, so2/λ−1+1/λ−1=2 givesλ=3/4 and the displayed allocation.

Compare the optimum with equal allocation(1,1) and concentrated allocation(2,0).

InR⁴ useh₀=(1,1,1,1)/2,h₁=(1,1,−1,−1)/2,h₂=(1,−1,0,0)/√2,h₃=(0,0,1,−1)/√2.

For a smooth bijectiong in Euclidean coordinates, defineT_gf(x)=|detDg⁻¹(x)|^{1/2}f(g⁻¹x).

The fourh_j are orthonormal, sof=Σ〈f,h_j〉h_j and the frame bounds areA=B=1. Two copies of everyh_j scaled by1/√2 give a redundant tight frame with the same bounds. T_g is unitary onL².

Direct dot products giveh_iᵀh_j=δ_ij, and four orthonormal vectors spanR⁴. Parseval and reconstruction follow. In the duplicate family each squared coefficient is halved but occurs twice, so their total remains||f||² andS=I; redundancy does not imply unique coefficients. A hyperbolic isometry preserves its invariant volume measure and needs no such Euclidean-coordinate correction once that measure is used consistently.

Apply the Haar transform tof=(0,1,2,3).

Which distribution statistic and production identity are actually being compared, and what assumptions determine each?

G is unchanged by multiplying every income by a positive constant. For(0,0,2,2),G=1/2; for(1,1,1,1),G=0. The production formula differentiates exactly todlogY=dlogA+αdlogK+βdlogL.

Revised question

How does optimizing a large parameter grid change the uncertainty of the selected score?

A finite-family concentration bound quantifies selection error under explicit independent bounded-data assumptions. It shows why a best synthetic Sharpe value is not a validated predictive result.

Definitions and assumptions

LetK fixed candidate models have lossesℓ_k(Z)∈[0,1] on independent identically distributed validation observationsZ₁,…,Z_n.

WriteR_k=Eℓ_k andR̂_k=n⁻¹Σℓ_k(Z_i). The candidates must be fixed independently of this validation sample for the elementary bound.

The recovered gridj_min,j_max,λ₁,λ₂,Q and500-ms sampling describe a search procedure, not an independence or boundedness theorem for market returns.

Uniform finite-family validation bound

With probability at least1−δ, every candidate satisfies|R̂_k−R_k|≤ε=√[log(2K/δ)/(2n)]. The empirically best candidate then has true risk at most2ε above the best candidate’s true risk.

Derivation or proof

Hoeffding’s inequality givesP(|R̂_k−R_k|>ε)≤2e^{−2nε²} for each fixed candidate. A union bound overK candidates gives2Ke^{−2nε²}; setting this equal toδ gives the radius. Ifk̂ minimizes empirical risk andk* minimizes true risk, thenR_k̂≤R̂_k̂+ε≤R̂_k*+ε≤R_k*+2ε. This is a complete selection argument under the assumptions, not an assertion that arbitrary rolling returns satisfy them. Fitting candidates on the same validation sample violates the fixed-family premise unless the entire possible family was already included inK.

Worked example

TakeK=1000,n=1000,δ=0.05.

The radius is approximately0.07279 and the excess-risk bound approximately0.14558. Increasing the number of searched combinations without more independent observations enlarges the uniform uncertainty. A Sharpe ratio also needs a nonzero variance denominator; a constant positive synthetic return makes its naive ratio undefined or infinite rather than exceptionally certified.

The revised optimization specifies an out-of-sample inferential guarantee and its limitations.

Scope

Actual time series can be dependent, nonstationary and heavy-tailed. This result is not financial guidance and does not certify a strategy. Synthetic signals test implementation behavior, not historical market performance.

Further development

Use a chronological training/validation/test split and an explicit dependence model. Derive a concentration or bootstrap procedure justified for that model and report the complete search family, costs and uncertainty of the final score. Reusing the validation sample adaptively changes the inference problem. A final untouched test set can evaluate the selected model after selection, but its confidence statement then concerns that fixed selected model, not a fresh search over the test data. Repeatedly checking and selecting on the final set destroys this separation.

Revised question

Which exact identities distinguish a creation algebra from a finite matrix approximation, and what does a Boolean Gaussian actually mean?

Prefix creation on word space satisfies Cuntz–Toeplitz relations with a vacuum defect. Separately, the Boolean moment–cumulant recursion makes a symmetric two-point law Gaussian in the Boolean sense, unlike the classical Gaussian.

Definitions and assumptions

Let the full word Hilbert space have orthonormal basis|w⟩ over finite words in two letters, including the empty vacuum. DefineL_i|w⟩=|iw⟩.

Boolean cumulantsb_n satisfy m₀=1 andm_n=Σ_{j=1}ⁿb_jm_{n−j}, equivalent to summing products over interval partitions.

These constructions require stated notions of independence; a word such as Itô does not transfer classical stochastic rules to a different probability theory.

L_i*L_j=δ_ijI andΣ_iL_iL_i*=I−P_vac. For a symmetric variableX=±1,m_{2n}=1,m_{2n+1}=0 and its only nonzero Boolean cumulant isb₂=1.

Derivation or proof

Removing the first letter undoes prefixing when the letters agree and kills it otherwise, proving the first relation. Every nonempty word begins with exactly one letter, while the vacuum lies in neither range, proving the defect formula. In a finite-dimensional space two exact isometries with orthogonal ranges cannot both exist: their ranges would each have the full ambient dimension. Finite truncations therefore add boundary defects. For cumulants, the moment series isM(z)=1/(1−z²). The recursion impliesM=1+B M, soB=1−1/M=z². Thus onlyb₂ survives. This does not give the classical Gaussian, whose fourth moment is three; the two-point law has fourth moment one.

Worked example

Inspect words of length at most two and compute the first six moments.

There are1+2+4=7 basis words. Prefixing and truncating annihilates length-two inputs, so its adjoint-product is notI on that top layer. The moment sequence is1,0,1,0,1,0,1; interval-pairing recursion reproduces it exactly.

The result supplies concrete algebra and probability instead of treating advanced operator names as interchangeable.

It does not construct a Cuntz–Pimsner market model or a Boolean stochastic differential equation. A stochastic integral and its Itô rule need their own Fock-space and adaptedness definitions.

Which monodromy condition can be checked for a concrete second-order equation, and why is unipotent monodromy still nontrivial?

A constant-potential equation on a periodic parameter has a complete monodromy calculation. The zero-potential case has only eigenvalue one but a nonidentity Jordan block, exposing a condition that spectral eigenvalues alone miss.

Consider y″=λy over a parameter interval of length one and writev=(y,y′). Thenv′=A_λv withA_λ=[[0,1],[λ,0]].

The monodromy isM_λ=e^{A_λ}; monodromy-free in this model meansM_λ=I.

This scalar constant-coefficient test is newly specified; a general oper includes geometric and gauge data not recovered here.

Complete constant-potential monodromy test

Forλ=−4π²n² with nonzero integern,M_λ=I. Forλ=0,M₀=[[1,1],[0,1]]≠I although both eigenvalues are one.

A_λ²=λI. Ifλ=−ω² withω≠0, the exponential isIcosω+(A_λ/ω)sinω. It is the identity whenω=2πn, giving the stated family. Atλ=0 the square ofA vanishes, so its exponential isI+A, proving the nontrivial unipotent case. For general complexλ≠0, diagonalization gives eigenvaluese^{±√λ}. Both are one only when√λ is a nonzero integer multiple of2πi, in which case the matrix is diagonalizable and isI. The exceptionalλ=0 case is precisely where that diagonalization fails; replacing matrix equality by eigenvalue equality loses it.

Compare initial datav(0)=(0,1) atλ=0 andλ=−4π².

At zero potential,y(t)=t andv(1)=(1,1), so the initial vector is not restored. Atλ=−4π²,y(t)=sin(2πt)/(2π) andv(1)=(0,1), restoring every solution’s data after one period.

The example supplies an exact monodromy condition rather than a label attached to an unspecified spectral support.

What does a heat trace measure in a finite model, and which analytic conditions are needed before a proposed operator is a spectral triple?

A four-cycle gives an exact scale-dependent heat dimension. A separate diagonal model shows that compact resolvent and finite heat trace do not imply finite-power zeta summability.

Definitions and assumptions

For the four-cycle graph Laplacian eigenvalues are0,2,2,4. SetP(t)=Tr(e^{−tL})/4 andd_s(t)=−2dlogP/dlogt.

For a diagonal positive operatorD with eigenvaluen of multiplicityd_n=ceil(e^{√n}), each eigenspace is finite dimensional.

A spectral-triple claim needs a represented algebra, a self-adjointD, compact resolvent and bounded commutators; its summability properties require additional estimates.

Exact heat dimension and a summability distinction

For the cycle,P(t)=(1+e^{−2t})²/4 andd_s(t)=8t/(e^{2t}+1), tending to zero at both ends. The diagonalD has compact resolvent andTr(e^{−tD})<∞ for everyt>0, butTr(D^{−p})=∞ for every finitep>0.

Derivation or proof

Sum the four heat eigenvalues and differentiate the logarithm to obtain the first formula. At smallt the numerator tends to zero; at larget exponential growth in the denominator dominates. ForD, eigenvalues tend to infinity with finite multiplicity, so the resolvent eigenvalues tend to zero and finite-rank truncations converge in norm. For fixedt>0,√n≤tn/2 for all sufficiently largen, givingd_ne^{−tn}≤2e^{−tn/2}, a convergent tail. Butd_n n^{−p} does not even tend to zero, so the power trace diverges. This example distinguishesθ-summability from finitep-summability without requiring a conjectural Monster spectrum.

Revised question

Which error family is corrected by an explicit code, and why must code distance be an integer rather than a fitted real constant?

The three-qubit repetition subspace corrects any single bit flip, but it does not correct a single phase flip and has quantum distance one. The exact distinction prevents classical redundancy from being reported as universal quantum protection.

Definitions and assumptions

LetC=span{|000⟩,|111⟩}, with projectorP. Consider errorsE={I,X₁,X₂,X₃}.

Knill–Laflamme requiresPE_a†E_bP=c_abP for the declared correctable error family.

A stabilizer code distance is the minimum integer weight of a nontrivial logical Pauli operator; it is not an arbitrary real expression√C.

Exact correction and exact uncorrectable error

For the four bit-flip errors,PE_a†E_bP=δ_abP, so they are jointly correctable. ButPZ₁P acts as logicaldiag(1,−1), not a scalar. Hence the code has parameters[[3,1,1]], despite its classical bit-flip distance three.

Derivation or proof

Ifa=b, the error product isI and the condition givesP. Ifa≠b, the product flips one or two distinct bits. Applied to either codeword it lands in a basis state orthogonal to both codewords, making the projected product zero. The four resulting error subspaces are mutually orthogonal and fill the eight-dimensional ambient space; measuring their syndrome and undoing the indicated flip gives recovery. A phase flipZ₁ leaves the basis strings in place but reverses the phase of|111⟩, so its restriction is a nontrivial logicalZ. This weight-one logical operator proves distance one. The distinction follows from the actual error action, not a code-size analogy.

Worked example

ApplyX₂ andZ₁ separately to(|000⟩+|111⟩)/√2.

X₂ gives(|010⟩+|101⟩)/√2 in a recognizable orthogonal syndrome subspace and is reversed byX₂. Z₁ gives(|000⟩−|111⟩)/√2 inside the original codespace, changing its encoded state while leaving the bit-flip syndrome trivial.

A code claim is now tied to an encoding and a checked error family.

The source’s large parameter expression[[196884,24,√C]] does not provide an encoding, integer distance or recovery theorem. The quantum Singleton bound is a necessary parameter check, not an existence proof.

Revised question

What does a specified completely positive update actually preserve, and which coherence decays under repetition?

The qubit depolarizing channel has an exact Kraus certificate and contraction factor. Trace preservation does not mean preservation of an input’s off-diagonal information or a claimed operational-coherence percentage.

Definitions and assumptions

For0≤p≤1 defineE_p(ρ)=(1−p)ρ+pI/2 on trace-one qubit matrices.

A Kraus representationE(ρ)=ΣK_jρK_j† is completely positive, andΣK_j†K_j=I gives trace preservation.

Trace distance isD(ρ,σ)=||ρ−σ||₁/2. Writeρ=(I+r·σ)/2 in Bloch coordinates.

Exact depolarizing contraction

Kraus operators are√(1−3p/4)I and√(p/4)X,Y,Z. The channel sendsr to(1−p)r and satisfiesD(E_p^nρ,E_p^nσ)=(1−p)^nD(ρ,σ).

Derivation or proof

The identityXρX+YρY+ZρZ=2Tr(ρ)I−ρ follows by expandingρ in the Pauli basis. Substituting the four Kraus terms gives(1−p)ρ+pI/2, and their squared coefficients sum to one, proving the channel properties. On a difference of two states the identity term cancels, soE_p(ρ−σ)=(1−p)(ρ−σ). Homogeneity of the trace norm proves the exact distance formula, with iteration giving its power. This is stronger and more specific than saying the update is coherent: it quantifies the information that is intentionally lost.

Worked example

Takep=1/5,ρ=|0⟩⟨0|,σ=|1⟩⟨1| andn=5.

Their initial trace distance is one; after five updates it is(4/5)^5=1024/3125≈0.32768. Each state approachesI/2. Off-diagonal input entries shrink by the same factor, so no nontrivial qubit coherence is exactly protected by this channel.

The update’s positivity, normalization and observability behavior have independent exact certificates.

Derivation or proof

Both states place probability one half on00 and11 and zero elsewhere. Every diagonal observable therefore has the same expectation. Partial trace removes the Bell cross terms, leaving the same marginalI/2. The operatorXX exchanges00 and11, so its expectation is the sum of those cross terms: one for the Bell state and zero for the mixture. Their difference is( |00⟩⟨11|+|11⟩⟨00| )/2, whose nonzero eigenvalues are±1/2. Its trace norm is one, giving distance one half. This proves that one class of observations can agree exactly while a different observable resolves the states.

It retains every stated diagonal statistic but hasXX expectation1/2. In fact the entire familyρ(q) with coherenceq/2,0≤q≤1, shares those diagonal observations whileXX readsq. Repeating only the diagonal measurements at greater precision cannot identifyq.

The mathematical issue is observation sufficiency, not merely the number of measurements.

Revised question

What does a rank-k reduction preserve, and which error can be certified before assigning speed claims?

The recovered tensor-processing proposal names SVD and rank reduction but gives no measured complexity certificate. The matrix problem has a sharp mathematical answer: singular values determine the best Frobenius error. This supplies a reproducible approximation statement independently of any hardware throughput.

Definitions and assumptions

Let A be an m×n real matrix with singular values s1≥s2≥…≥0. The Frobenius norm squares and sums all entries.

A rank-k approximation is a matrix B with rank at mostk; arithmetic cost and approximation error are different quantities.

Truncated SVD optimality

The minimum of ||A−B||_F² over rank(B)≤k isΣ_(j>k)s_j², attained by retaining the firstk singular terms.

Derivation or proof

LetP be the orthogonal projection onto the column space ofB, with rank at mostk. Decompose A−B=(I−P)A+(PA−B); the two summands have orthogonal column spaces, so its squared norm is at least||(I−P)A||_F²=Tr(AAᵀ)−Tr(PAAᵀ). In an eigenbasis ofAAᵀ the latter trace isΣs_j²p_jj, where0≤p_jj≤1 andΣp_jj≤k. Its maximum is the sum of the k largest squared singular values. This proves the lower bound. TakingB=Σ_(j≤k)s_ju_jv_jᵀ attains it, completing the proof including ties.

Worked example

Use A=diag(5,3,1).

Its total squared norm is35. The optimal rank-one matrixdiag(5,0,0) has error9+1=10, and rank two has error1. A relative squared error below1/20 requires rank two, since10/35>1/20 but1/35<1/20.

The retained rank can now be chosen from a declared error target, rather than from a headline reduction factor.

Scope

The theorem concerns a matrix and the Frobenius norm. A tensor’s chosen unfolding can change the ranks, and a matrix error bound does not directly certify a downstream control or topology decision.

What assumptions justify the recovered event-response formula and how can its rate be checked?

LetN(t) be a Poisson process of rateλ>0 andT=inf{t:N(t)≥1}.

Its survival probability isS(t)=P(T>t); the hazard rate ish(t)=−d(logS(t))/dt.

Arrival probability and rate identification

The eventT>t isN(t)=0. The Poisson mass formula givesP(N(t)=0)=e^(−λt), establishing the distribution. The tail integralE[T]=∫₀∞P(T>t)dt equals1/λ. DifferentiatinglogS yields the constant hazard, and solvingS(t)=1−p gives the identification formula. The memoryless identityP(T>s+t|T>s)=S(s+t)/S(s)=S(t) follows immediately. Conversely a claimed model whose conditional waiting probability depends on past waiting time is not this homogeneous arrival law.

Useλ=2 in inverse-time units.

The median solvese^(−2t)=1/2, sot_med=(log2)/2, whereas the mean is1/2. At that median, the probability of at least two events is1−e^(−λt)(1+λt)=(1−log2)/2. First-arrival probability and event count are therefore different observables.

The model yields exact quantities that can be compared with data only after the event and time unit are defined.

What metric follows from an explicitly defined finite spectral triple?

The recovered spectral-triple proposal contains a formal commutator expansion but no concrete operator domain. A two-point triple has no domain ambiguity and yields a complete distance calculation. It also shows directly how rescalingD changes the metric.

Definitions and assumptions

RepresentA=C⊕C diagonally onH=C², and letD=[[0,m],[conj(m),0]] withm≠0.

For the two evaluation statesδ1,δ2, define d(δ1,δ2)=sup{|a−b|:a,b real,||[D,diag(a,b)]||≤1}.

Two-point spectral distance

The distance equals1/|m|. Ifm=0 the distance is infinite.

Derivation or proof

The commutator has off-diagonal entriesm(b−a) andconj(m)(a−b). Its adjoint times itself is|m|²(a−b)²I, so its operator norm is|m||a−b|. The constraint is therefore exactly|a−b|≤1/|m|, and equality is attained by a suitable real diagonal element. Ifm=0, every commutator vanishes while|a−b| is unbounded, giving infinite distance. All spectral-triple conditions in this finite setting are immediate: the algebra is represented by bounded operators,D is self-adjoint, and its resolvent is compact becauseH is finite-dimensional. A formal gradient approximation was unnecessary.

Takem=2 and then replaceD by3D.

The distances are1/2 and1/6. The two-point set and its algebra are unchanged, yet the metric changes. Conversely, choosingm purely imaginary with the same modulus leaves the distance unchanged because the operator norm depends only on|m|.

The operator supplies concrete metric information that is not determined by the algebra’s name alone.

A one-dimensional formal group lawF(x,y) is an associative commutative power series withidentity0. Its[p]_F(x) addsx to itselfp times.

Over a field of characteristicp, finite heighth means the first nonzero term of[p]_F has degreep^h; if[p]_F=0 the height is infinite.

ForF_m(x,y)=x+y+xy, [p](x)=(1+x)^p−1, reducing tox^p in characteristicp, so its height is1. The additive lawF_a=x+y has[p]=px=0 in characteristicp and infinite height.

In characteristicp, the binomial theorem removes all intermediate coefficients becausep divides binomial(p,j) for0<j<p, leavingx^p. The additive calculation is immediate. Thus two simple formal groups over the same characteristic have different heights. An invertible coordinate changeg(x)=ux+O(x²),u≠0, conjugates the p-series and preserves the lowest nonzero exponent, so this distinction is intrinsic to the formal-group isomorphism class.

Revised question

Reconstruction: Which Gaussian derivative gives a consistent Mexican-hat Fourier pair, what moments vanish, and what admissibility integral follows?

The external May4 file contains a Mexican-hat formula and Fourier transform that do not match under the usual unnormalized forward transform. This repair fixes the convention before proving cancellation and admissibility. The file context is retained as T; no historical user prompt or completed wavelet theorem is invented.

Definitions and assumptions

Use F[f](ω)=∫_R f(x)e^(−iωx)dx. Let Gσ(x)=(√(2π)σ)^(−1)e^(−x²/(2σ²)), σ>0, so F[Gσ]=e^(−σ²ω²/2).

Define ψσ=−Gσ″=(√(2π)σ³)^(−1)(1−x²/σ²)e^(−x²/(2σ²)). These functions and their derivatives decay rapidly.

A consistent pair, two vanishing moments and finite admissibility

F[ψσ](ω)=ω²e^(−σ²ω²/2), ∫ψσ=∫xψσ=0, and ∫_R|F[ψσ](ω)|²/|ω|dω=σ^(−4). The source coefficient 1/(2πσ³) would instead give an extra factor 1/√(2π) with this transform convention.

Derivation or proof

Integration by parts gives F[f″]=−ω²F[f] when boundary terms vanish; apply it to Gσ. Integrating −Gσ″ directly gives zero. Integrating −xGσ″ by parts also gives zero because the remaining integral is a boundary difference of Gσ. Thus the Fourier transform vanishes to second order at frequency zero. For admissibility, symmetry reduces the integral to 2∫₀∞ω³e^(−σ²ω²)dω. With u=σ²ω² this is σ^(−4)∫₀∞ue^(−u)du=σ^(−4). All integrations converge absolutely. Finally the ratio of the source’s spatial coefficient to the corrected one is 1/√(2π); linearity of the transform forces the same ratio on the frequency side. A different Fourier convention could change constants, but it must be stated consistently on both sides.

Worked example

Take σ=1 and compare the corrected wavelet with the retrieved spatial coefficient.

The corrected value at zero is 1/√(2π), and the retrieved value is 1/(2π). The corrected frequency response at ω=1 is e^(−1/2), whereas the retrieved spatial normalization transforms to e^(−1/2)/√(2π). The admissibility integral is exactly one. The verifier evaluates Gaussian moments independently to check the two cancellations and checks the analytic normalization ratio.

Definitions and assumptions

Let K be a nonarchimedean valued field with additive valuation v, so v(xy)=v(x)+v(y) and v(x+y)≥min(v(x),v(y)). Set v(0)=∞.

If one of three nonzero summands has strictly smaller valuation than the other two, the sum of the other two has larger valuation and cannot cancel it. Therefore x+y+1=0 forces a repeated minimum. Enumerating which two entries attain it gives the three rays. Conversely, interpreting the rays as the complete tropical variety requires a lifting theorem over a suitable valued algebraic closure; only the elementary necessary condition is used here. The loss of unit data is concrete: over Q₃, (x,y)=(1,−2) lies on X and has valuations (0,0), while (1,1) has the same valuations but gives x+y+1=3≠0. Thus one valuation pair supports both an actual solution and a nonsolution depending on the leading units.

The first has valuation (0,0), the second (1,0); each has a repeated minimum and exactly satisfies the equation. The transitive closure of a relation declares two points equivalent whenever a finite chain of related points connects them.

The tolerance relation is not transitive. Its transitive closure on Q is the universal relation, so quotienting by that closure identifies every rational number, including zero and one.

A quotient with0=1 is not a field under the usual nontrivial-field axiom. Merely closing the relation under transitivity does not repair the intended numerical information; it erases it.

A fitted score and a theorem about unseen samples are different mathematical objects. The source’s spectral PAC–Bayes claim does not provide its prior, posterior, sample law or loss bound. Definitions and assumptions

Let H be finite, P a strictly positive prior fixed independently of an iid sample of size m, and ℓ(h,z)∈[0,1]. Define population loss L(h), empirical loss Lhat(h), and KL(Q||P)=ΣQ(h)log[Q(h)/P(h)].

Fix λ>0 andδ∈(0,1) before seeing the sample. Write L(Q),Lhat(Q) for posterior averages.

A fixed-parameter PAC–Bayes–Hoeffding bound

With probability at least1−δ, simultaneously for every posterior Q, L(Q)≤Lhat(Q)+[KL(Q||P)+log(1/δ)]/λ+λ/(8m). This is a theorem under the declared iid bounded-loss model, not a consequence of R² or a spectral fit.

Derivation or proof

Hoeffding’s bounded-variable lemma gives E_sample exp(λ[L(h)−Lhat(h)])≤exp(λ²/(8m)) for each h. Average over the fixed prior and apply Markov: with probability at least1−δ, log E_P exp(λ[L−Lhat])≤λ²/(8m)+log(1/δ). For any finite probability Q, Jensen’s inequality applied after writing the prior sum using Q gives λE_Q(L−Lhat)≤KL(Q||P)+log E_P exp(λ[L−Lhat]). Combining proves the bound uniformly in Q on that one event. Zero posterior masses are handled by continuity. Optimizing λ after observing Q requires a separate uniformization or parameter grid; the fixed-λ theorem does not silently supply it.

Worked example

Choose two hypotheses with uniform prior, a point-mass posterior, m=100,δ=.05,λ=20 and empirical loss.1.

Then KL=log2 and the penalty is log40/20+20/800≈.2094439727, giving L(Q)≤.3094439727 on the stated event. Separately R²=1−SSE/SST only describes squared errors on its evaluated response set; the number.847 omits the response normalization, split and dependency assumptions needed to connect it with this theorem.

The proof makes its probability event, optimization domain and constants reviewable, while preserving the empirical report as a claim rather than a verified forecast.

Scope

Prime-indexed observations are not automatically iid. Unbounded squared loss is outside the bounded-loss theorem unless explicitly controlled. A data-dependent prior needs another theorem. No cryptographic or cross-domain benefit follows from this certificate.

Further development

Specify a dependency model, bounded or tail-controlled loss and a prior independent of the held-out data. A spectral hypothesis can enter only through a proved complexity or KL estimate, after which the actual numerical bound should be reported alongside the score.

Revised question

Reconstruction: Which multiplicative convolution is intended, when do transforms turn it into a product, and what exact arithmetic identity can an implementation certify?

The historical report’s multiplicative-function approximation and inversion claims lack their actual kernel and norms. The classical divisor convolution gives a well-defined replacement. It proves an exact transform product when absolute convergence permits regrouping, rather than asserting a universal approximation capability.

Definitions and assumptions

For arithmetic functions f,g:N→C, define(f*g)(n)=Σ_{d|n}f(d)g(n/d). Let1(n)=1 and ε(1)=1, ε(n)=0 for n>1.

A function is multiplicative if f(mn)=f(m)f(n) for coprime m,n and f(1)=1. Its Dirichlet series is D_f(s)=Σf(n)n^(−s) where absolutely convergent.

Convolution, inversion and a transform product

Dirichlet convolution is associative and commutative with identity ε. The Möbius function satisfies μ*1=ε. Whenever D_f,D_g converge absolutely, D_(f*g)(s)=D_f(s)D_g(s). Multiplicative inputs give a multiplicative convolution.

Derivation or proof

Associativity follows by writing either parenthesization as the finite sum overabc=n of f(a)g(b)h(c); commutativity swaps complementary divisors. For μ, summing μ(d) over divisors of n factors as∏_{p|n}(1−1), zero unless n=1. The Dirichlet-series product is the absolutely convergent double sumΣ_{a,b}f(a)g(b)(ab)^(−s); group terms by n=ab to obtain the formula. For coprime m,n, each divisor of mn decomposes uniquely into a divisor of m times a divisor of n, so the convolution sum factors. These are concrete algebraic and analytic hypotheses, not consequences of a neural architecture name.

Worked example

Take f=g=1, then invert the divisor-count function τ=1*1 by μ.

τ(12)=6 from divisors1,2,3,4,6,12. The identity μ*τ=1 gives at12 the sum τ(12)−τ(6)−τ(4)+τ(2)=6−4−3+2=1. Consequently the absolutely convergent series of τ is ζ(s)² for Re(s)>1. The verifier checks the convolution and inversion on every integer through120.

A finite implementation can certify these exact arithmetic identities while leaving approximation and extrapolation claims separate.

Scope

This does not prove exponential approximation of arbitrary multiplicative functions, inversion of a noisy learned transform, or a number-theoretic theorem from finite training. Other notions of multiplicative convolution, such as Haar convolution on R_+, need different definitions.

Substitution yields the strain formula and equal-layer stresses. If both layers were externally constrained toε=0, the stresses would instead be−E_iα_iΔT, showing why omitted compatibility data cannot be repaired by a more precise multiplication. The stress dimensions are modulus times dimensionless strain; expansion coefficients carry inverse-temperature units.

Revised question

Reconstruction: What group action is actually realized by signed coordinate reflections on F₃⁴, and can it be identified with exceptional Weyl groups without further data?

The program description names B₄,E₆,E₇,E₈ and coordinate reflections. Signed coordinate permutations give a genuine B₄ action with an exact finite classification. Names of exceptional groups do not make them the same representation, and their orders already rule out some proposed faithful linear identifications.

Definitions and assumptions

Let B₄ be the group of signed4×4 permutation matrices over F₃. Each sign is±1, distinct in this field. It acts on the81 vectors in F₃⁴.

Hamming weight w(x) is the number of nonzero coordinates. The reduced quadratic sumΣx_i² equals w(x) modulo three, a coarser invariant.

Order, orbits and a faithful-representation obstruction

|B₄|=2⁴·4!=384. Its orbits are exactly the five Hamming-weight classes, of sizes1,8,24,32,16. A faithful linear action of W(E₈) on F₃⁴ is impossible because|W(E₈)|=696729600 exceeds|GL₄(F₃)|=24261120.

Derivation or proof

Choose a permutation of the four coordinates and an independent sign for each output coordinate; the resulting384 matrices are distinct. They preserve the number of nonzero coordinates. Conversely any vector of weight r can be moved to(1,…,1,0,…,0) by a permutation and sign flips, proving one orbit for each r. Choose its support in binomial(4,r) ways and its nonzero signs in2^r ways, giving the sizes. Their sum is81. For the obstruction, a faithful linear action embeds its group into GL₄(F₃). Counting ordered independent columns gives(81−1)(81−3)(81−9)(81−27)=24261120, too small for W(E₈). The quoted E₈ order is a classical root-system input; the cardinality contradiction is elementary.

Worked example

Compare vectors(1,0,0,0) and(1,1,1,1).

Both have quadratic sum one modulo three, but their Hamming weights one and four put them in different B₄ orbits. The verifier enumerates all81 vectors and all384 signed permutations, checking the orbit partition exactly. It also checks the GL order and the order obstruction.

A complete finite group-action result replaces a loose exceptional-group label without claiming a review of unrecovered source code.

Scope

A nonfaithful action or a higher-dimensional exceptional representation is not excluded. The finite orbit calculation establishes no L-function, modularity, mirror-symmetry or deductive proof capability.

Further development

Supply actual generator matrices for every claimed group and verify defining relations, group order and faithfulness. Compare orbit invariants only after that representation certificate is complete.

Revised question

What does the literal avoidance complex encode, and is the claimed universal2-SAT topology correct?

The early July project proposed a homological complexity hierarchy. Its simplicial construction can be made coherent, but its asserted topological classification needs independent proof. Even the empty2-CNF formula provides a decisive counterexample to universal contractibility.

Definitions and assumptions

For n Boolean variables use vertices x_i,¬x_i. A face contains no opposite pair and no set consisting of all negated literals of a clause. A full face chooses exactly one literal per variable; it represents the corresponding truth assignment. Reduced homology uses an explicitly chosen coefficient field.

Satisfying facets and a counterexample

Full(n−1)-dimensional faces correspond exactly to satisfying assignments. With no clauses, the complex is the join of n two-point sets, the boundary of the n-dimensional crosspolytope, homeomorphic to S^(n−1). It is not contractible for n≥1.

Derivation or proof

A full face satisfies a clause precisely when it does not choose all the clause’s negations. Applying that test to every clause proves the assignment correspondence. With no clauses, only opposite-pair exclusions remain. Each variable contributes a choice of either endpoint of a0-sphere, and joining these choices gives the crosspolytope boundary. Its reduced homology in degree n−1 is one-dimensional. The formula with no clauses is a valid2-CNF formula and is trivially satisfiable, yet has nontrivial topology. Therefore neither satisfiability nor ease of decision implies contractibility for this construction. An entropy or Betti profile may still be studied as an observable, but cannot inherit a complexity theorem from its name.

Worked example

Use two variables and no clauses.

The vertices x,¬x,y,¬y form a four-cycle with edges joining choices from different variables. It has four vertices,four edges and no triangles, so β₁=1. Adding suitable clauses can delete faces and change the topology without establishing a monotone decision-complexity scale.

The construction survives, while the universal2-SAT/HCH classification fails for an explicit simplest input.

Scope

This does not settle any relation between topology and worst-case complexity. A filtration and an allowed reduction class must be defined before persistence or hierarchy claims are meaningful.

Further development

Fix a functorial construction and test which reductions actually preserve or reflect the chosen homology; state resulting implications as theorems or explicit conjectures.

Revised question

Which part of the3-SAT-to-CLIQUE construction is proved, and what extra condition would make its homology map injective?

The July2 response conjectured homology injectivity from a standard decision reduction. Correctness of a reduction concerns the existence of solutions, whereas injectivity concerns every cycle and boundary. These are different statements, and a small simplicial map shows the gap.

Definitions and assumptions

For a k-clause formula, create one graph vertex per literal occurrence. Join vertices from different clauses when their literals are not contradictory. A simplicial map sends vertices to vertices and every face to a face; repeated images may lower dimension.

The standard clique equivalence and the missing topological theorem

The formula is satisfiable exactly when the occurrence graph has a k-clique. A simplicial map in general need not induce an injective homology map, even when it preserves an existence predicate.

Derivation or proof

A satisfying assignment chooses a true literal in each clause. The chosen occurrences are pairwise noncontradictory and lie in different clauses, hence form a k-clique. Conversely a k-clique contains one occurrence from each clause, since no same-clause vertices are adjacent. Its literals are consistent and extend to a full satisfying assignment. Nothing in this argument constructs a chain-level retraction or proves a nonzero cycle survives. For a counterexample to automatic injectivity, map every vertex of a simplicial circle to one vertex. This is a valid simplicial map and induces the zero map H₁(S¹)→H₁(point)=0. An injective vertex map also would not suffice if the target fills a cycle with new two-simplices.

Worked example

Map the boundary of a triangle into the filled triangle by inclusion.

The source has H₁≅F and the target H₁=0, so even an inclusion of simplicial complexes can kill homology. A genuine homology embedding needs a separate argument such as a chain retraction or a suitable relative-homology criterion.

The decision reduction remains valid; the claimed obstruction hierarchy requires substantially more than that equivalence.

Scope

NoP-versus-NP separation or no-reduction theorem follows. Historical PHP Betti numbers are not adopted without their actual complex and boundary matrices.

Further development

Build the proposed chain maps explicitly and either construct a left inverse up to homotopy or exhibit a cycle that is killed.

Revised question

Which union-closed families admit a direct half-frequency proof, and what do small enumerations establish?

The July2 project studied Frankl’s conjecture with topological summaries and empirical counts. A simple injection gives a genuine theorem for a broad subclass. Exhaustive small-universe checks can then be certified, while correlations and reported Betti values remain distinct evidence.

Definitions and assumptions

A finite family F of subsets is union-closed if A∪B∈F whenever A,B∈F. Frankl’s conjecture asks whether every nontrivial finite such family has an element belonging to at least half its sets. Assume the union of the family is nonempty.

Singleton certificate

If{a}∈F, then a belongs to at least|F|/2 members of F. The map A↦A∪{a} injects the members not containing a into those containing a.

Derivation or proof

Union closure puts A∪{a} in F. If A and B both omit a and their unions with{a} agree, removing a gives A=B, proving injectivity. Thus the number omitting a is at most the number containing it, exactly the desired inequality. This proof makes no use of a topology or an entropy. It also explains its limitation: a family with no singleton does not admit this particular injection automatically. A complete search on a fixed finite universe can test all families by exact unions and frequencies, but it cannot prove the unbounded conjecture. Reported small Betti vectors additionally require the actual associated complex and coefficient convention.

Worked example

Use F={∅,{1},{1,2},{1,3},{1,2,3}}.

This family is union-closed and contains{1}. Four of its five sets contain1. The only set omitting1 is∅, whose injection image is{1}. A portable checker can independently enumerate every family on three labels and verify the frequency statement for that finite scope.

The exact injection is a theorem; finite enumeration is a bounded certificate; neither is replaced by a topology–complexity correlation.

Scope

No general solution of Frankl’s conjecture is claimed. The historical n=4,n=5 counts depend on an unrecovered critical-strip selection rule and are not reproduced as facts.

Further development

Specify the selected family class and seek an explicit injection or compression argument that applies beyond the singleton case.

Revised question

Which graph measure defines the curvature, and can a computed value justify a complexity or cryptographic claim?

The July3–4 frameworks used curvature, spectral gaps and Betti numbers as proposed difficulty indicators. Those observables require precise constructions. A complete elementary transport calculation shows how curvature depends on the chosen neighborhood measure, while no security or hardness theorem is inferred.

Definitions and assumptions

For adjacent vertices x,y at graph distance one, choose probability measures m_x,m_y and define κ(x,y)=1−W₁(m_x,m_y). W₁ minimizesΣd(u,v)π(u,v) over couplings with the declared marginals. Here use the uniform measure on neighbors, with no idleness.

Exact curvatures of two small graphs

For K₂ the unique edge has κ=0. For K₃ every edge has κ=1/2 under this measure convention.

Derivation or proof

In K₂, the neighbor measures are point masses at opposite endpoints, so transporting unit mass costs one. In K₃ with vertices x,y,z, the measures are(δ_y+δ_z)/2 and(δ_x+δ_z)/2. Match the common z-mass to itself and move the remaining half from y to x, costing1/2. This is optimal because the target has half a unit at x and the source has none there; all possible source points are distance one from x. Hence W₁=1/2. A different idleness convention changes the measures and can change κ, so comparison requires locked definitions. Similarly complex cochain coefficients do not by themselves create new quantum Betti numbers: for integer boundary matrices the ranks over Q and C agree.

Worked example

Compare the two degree patterns.

K₂ gives curvature zero and K₃ positive curvature despite both being trivial finite decision inputs. The value describes transport geometry of the chosen graph, not a proved attack cost or a worst-case complexity class.

A mathematically defined observable can be computed exactly while its intended predictive interpretation remains unsupported.

Scope

The direct-sum sequence splits by its coordinate inclusion. Their Ext dimension is identical because endpoints are identical.

Compare the two middle modules R and k⊕k.

In R the nilpotent ε acts nontrivially, linking the two factors; on k⊕k it acts as zero. Both have vector-space dimension two, so dimensions alone cannot distinguish the extension. The actual obstruction is the zero or nonzero class in Ext¹.

Which merge law makes duplicate and reordered messages harmless, and what remains undecided for concurrent events?

Each identity reduces coordinatewise to the corresponding elementary maximum identity. If z bounds x and y, every z_i≥max(x_i,y_i), proving leastness. Revised question

How do parameter uncertainty and simulation error differ in a finite reliability model?

The proposal named Bayesian risk and Monte Carlo disruption models without a recovered dataset. A fully stipulated Bernoulli model yields exact posterior predictions and reveals dependence caused by a shared unknown parameter.

Definitions and assumptions

Let p have Beta(1,1) prior and let observations be independent Bernoulli(p) conditional on p. After s successes and f failures the posterior is Beta(s+1,f+1). No actual reliability measurements are inferred here.

Posterior moments govern joint predictions

After three successes and one failure, E[p]=2/3 and E[p²]=10/21. Two future successes therefore have probability10/21, exceeding the plug-in value4/9 by2/63.

Derivation or proof

The likelihood multiplies the uniform prior by p³(1−p), giving Beta(4,2). Beta-integral ratios give E[p]=4/6 and E[p²]=4·5/(6·7). Conditional independence yields P(X₁=X₂=1|p)=p²; averaging uses E[p²], not(E[p])². The difference is Var(p)=2/63 and represents parameter uncertainty. Separately, for N independent Bernoulli simulations at a fixed stipulated probability, Hoeffding’s inequality gives P(|p̂−p|≥ε)≤2exp(−2Nε²). That bound controls simulation sampling error under the model, not the model’s adequacy or posterior uncertainty. It cannot justify independence of actual failures.

Worked example

Compare exact prediction with a separate fixed-probability simulation target ε=0.05,δ=0.05.

The posterior two-success probability is0.476190…, while plug-in independence gives0.444444…. The Hoeffding sample bound is N≥ceil(log40/(2·0.05²))=738 for the separate simulation problem.

A simulation may be accurate about an assumed model while uncertainty in its parameter remains substantial.

Which quantities are actually defined, and do the supplied numbers support the proposed exponential law?

The July28 framework assigned densities to Lie/sporadic pairs, cohomology degrees and a beta function. The numerical and logical claims can be audited without endorsing a new geometry. Definitions and independent predictions must precede a fitted law.

Definitions and assumptions

Use the stated ranks4,6,7,8 and densities9240,1320,80960,1020096. Let y_i=log₁₀density_i and proposed prediction0.514r_i+1.291. The symbol Λ_g and any density denominator still require definitions.

A direct residual test and a nonuniqueness theorem

The supplied line does not fit the first two densities closely: their residuals are about0.619 and−1.254 logarithmic units. Three beta values determine no unique function, even within smooth functions.

Evaluate the line at each rank and subtract from the logarithm of the stated density. A residual of−1.254 means the proposed value is too large by a factor about10^1.254, so it cannot be hidden by decimal rounding. For the beta claim, let P be the quadratic interpolant through its three stipulated inputs1/2,1,2. Every P(x)+c(x−1/2)(x−1)(x−2), c∈R, agrees at all three points and generally differs elsewhere. Likewise2+3+4+5=14 adds degree labels; it is not a computation of dimH²+dimH³+dimH⁴+dimH⁵, whose summands are Betti numbers that must be obtained from actual spaces.

Revised question

What Galois groups are even possible for the two recovered quartic polynomials?

The July28 framework associated quartics with M₁₂ and M₂₄. A degree bound already rules out a literal identification of their splitting-field Galois groups. The quartics themselves are legitimate algebraic objects whose irreducibility can be checked exactly.

Definitions and assumptions

Let f=x⁴−4x³+1 and h=x⁴−6x³+4x²+2x+1. A characteristic-zero splitting-field group acts faithfully by permutations of the four roots, hence embeds in S₄ and has order at most24.

Irreducible quartics with small possible Galois groups

Both f and h are irreducible over Q, but neither can have splitting-field group M₁₂ or M₂₄. A separate construction would be needed to relate their roots to a Mathieu representation.

Derivation or proof

A rational root of either monic polynomial with constant1 must be±1, and direct substitution excludes both. A remaining factorization would be two monic integral quadratics by Gauss’s lemma. Their constant terms must both be e=1 or both e=−1. Write(x²+ax+e)(x²+bx+e). Its cubic coefficient is a+b and linear coefficient e(a+b). For f these would have to be−4 and0, impossible for e=±1. For h they would have to be−6 and2, likewise impossible. Hence both are irreducible. Independently, any automorphism fixing all four roots fixes the splitting field they generate, proving the faithful S₄ embedding. The Mathieu groups have orders greater than24, excluding them without numerical root fitting.

Worked example

Check the constant/cubic/linear factor constraints.

For f, e(a+b)=±4 can never be0. For h it is±6 and never2. This proof does not determine whether the actual transitive subgroup is S₄,A₄,D₄,C₄ or V₄; discriminant and resolvent tests are still needed.

A degree-four formula may participate in a larger representation, but its literal root-permutation group obeys an unavoidable degree bound.

Scope

No Mathieu action or field discriminant was recovered. Polynomial discriminants, splitting fields and unrelated Pell fields must remain distinct.

Further development

Compute exact discriminants and cubic resolvents, then identify each actual transitive subgroup and state any additional representation map explicitly.

Revised question

How does searching many modular-coordinate fits change the interpretation of the best apparent anomaly?

The source moonshine interpretation selected fitted coordinates and reported a significance value. A finite family of tests gives an exact mathematical benchmark for distinguishing one prespecified statistic from a selected maximum.

Definitions and assumptions

Let p1,...,pM be valid null p-values, so Pr(pj<=u)<=u for each j.

Define p_adj=min(1,M*min_j pj). Independence is not assumed for the familywise bound.

Finite-search familywise control

Pr(p_adj<=alpha)<=alpha. If the p-values are independent uniform variables, Pr(min pj<=u)=1-(1-u)^M exactly.

Derivation or proof

The event p_adj<=alpha is contained in the union of events pj<=alpha/M. The union bound gives probability at most sum_j alpha/M=alpha, proving the adjusted test. Under independence, the complementary event pj>u for all j has probability(1-u)^M, giving the exact formula. The theorem concerns the whole specified search family: fitting extra parameters, choosing observables after inspection or retaining only successful seeds enlarges that family or requires a different null calibration. A held-out evaluation can avoid reusing the same observations for both selection and confirmation.

Worked example

As a newly stipulated illustration, take M=1000 independent null tests and u=0.001.

The chance of at least one such small p-value is1-0.999^1000, approximately0.6323. Thus a selected value0.001 does not carry the interpretation of one prespecified test.

The cost of selection can be computed without asserting any physical mechanism or interpreting fitted couplings as predictions.

Scope

The exact independence formula is illustrative. The historical search size, data covariance and original analysis are unavailable, so no corrected historical significance is claimed.

Further development

Freeze the observables and coordinate map, simulate the complete selection procedure under a stated correlated null, and compare a separately held-out statistic with that calibrated distribution.

Revised question

Which combination involving E2(9*tau) is genuinely modular, and why does its anomalous term cancel?

The CP-moonshine manuscript used E2(9*tau) as an analytic lift. A scalar weight-two example gives an exact covariance benchmark before introducing unknown triplet representations or fitted physics parameters.

Definitions and assumptions

Use E2(tau)=1-24 sum(n>=1)sigma1(n)q^n with q=exp(2pi*i*tau).

For N>1 define F_N(tau)=E2(tau)-N*E2(N*tau). For gamma in Gamma0(N), c is divisible by N.

Cancellation of the quasimodular anomaly

F_N transforms with weight2 on Gamma0(N). Its holomorphic modular-form extension at the cusps is the standard weight-two Eisenstein construction.

Derivation or proof

The classical formula is E2(gamma*tau)=(c*tau+d)²E2(tau)+[6/(pi*i)]c(c*tau+d). Since c is divisible by N, the integral matrix gamma_N=(a,Nb;c/N,d) lies in SL2(Z) and satisfies N*gamma*tau=gamma_N*(N*tau). Applying the same transformation to E2(N*gamma*tau) gives anomaly[6/(pi*i)](c/N)(c*tau+d). Multiplication by N makes this anomaly identical to the first one, so their difference vanishes. Holomorphy at cusps follows from the standard Eisenstein-series construction; the displayed calculation proves the covariance directly. It also shows why E2(N*tau) alone does not have the claimed homogeneous weight-two law.

Worked example

Take N=9 and compute the constant and q^9 coefficients.

The constant is1-9=-8. Since sigma1(9)=13, the q^9 coefficient is-24*13+216*1=-96; the q coefficient is-24. The nonzero constant term means this example is not a cusp form.

Do the finite TL relations and a declared trace actually define a positive inner product?

The August9 synthesis used Temperley–Lieb, Markov traces and thermodynamics together. A two-strand calculation isolates a necessary positivity condition. It does not claim that a condition sufficient for this small algebra is sufficient for every level of a TL tower.

For x=a+be, tr(x*x)=|a|²+2Re(overline a b)/δ+|b|². It is positive semidefinite exactly when|δ|≥1, and positive definite when|δ|>1.

At higher TL levels additional positivity restrictions arise; passing one finite Gram test cannot justify a full C*-tower or KMS identification. Compare δ=2 and δ=1/2.

Atδ=2 the Gram eigenvalues are3/2 and1/2. Atδ=1/2, x=1−e has tr(x*x)=2−2/δ=−2, so this cannot be a squared Hilbert norm.

Revised question

Which normalization turns an adjacency matrix into a stochastic transition matrix, and why does its entropy equal logλ?

The August9 PF/KMS discussion can be grounded in a finite primitive adjacency matrix. Its Perron eigenvectors define an exact stationary Markov chain. A relative-entropy calculation proves the relevant variational statement for this specified class of chains.

P is stochastic,π is stationary, and its entropy rate is logλ. Every stationary Markov chain Q supported on the same allowed edges has entropy rate at most logλ.

The PF equations giveΣ_jP_ij=1 andΣ_iπ_iP_ij=π_j. On allowed edges logP_ij=logr_j−logr_i−logλ. Averaging with stationary edge weightsπ_iP_ij cancels the r terms, giving−Σπ_iP_ijlogP_ij=logλ. Use A=[[1,1],[1,0]] and φ=(1+√5)/2.

Take r=(φ,1),ℓ=r/(φ²+1). Then P=[[1/φ,1/φ²],[1,0]], andπ=(φ²,1)/(φ²+1). The entropy rate is logφ. A KMS inverse-temperature interpretation requires a separately specified algebra and time evolution.

The normalization, stationary law and pressure value are explicit rather than conflated.

Revised question

Which covariance condition turns cylinder data into an actual Hilbert-valued random variable?

The August9 synthesis invoked Sazonov and Minlos. A diagonal Hilbert-space construction proves a concrete sufficient condition and exhibits the failure of identity covariance. This keeps a genuine measure theorem separate from formal consistency or category names.

Definitions and assumptions

Let H=ℓ² with basis e_n and independent standard normals Z_n. For q_n≥0 consider X=Σ√q_nZ_ne_n. The covariance has diagonal entries q_n.

Trace-summable construction and identity-covariance failure

IfΣq_n<∞, X converges almost surely in H and in mean square, with characteristic function exp(−Σq_nh_n²/2). For q_n=1 the coordinate law givesℓ² probability zero.

Derivation or proof

The nonnegative random sum S=Σq_nZ_n² has expectationΣq_n by monotone convergence. Finite expectation implies S<∞ almost surely, which is exactly square summability of the coordinates. The tail mean-square error equalsΣ_{n>N}q_n, proving L² convergence. Finite Gaussian characteristic functions multiply, and dominated convergence yields the displayed limit. The resulting Borel probability on the Polish spaceℓ² is Radon. By contrast the strong law gives N⁻¹Σ_{n≤N}Z_n²→1 almost surely when q_n=1, forcing divergence of the squared norm. Consistency of all finite marginals remains true, but their product measure is supported outsideℓ².

Worked example

Choose q_n=2^(−n),n≥1.

The covariance trace and E||X||² are one. Truncation after N has squared mean error2^(−N). Identity-covariance truncations have expected squared norm N and their probability of lying in any fixed-radius ball tends to zero.

Support and tightness, not just finite consistency, are the decisive missing hypotheses.

Scope

This proves the diagonal case, not the general Sazonov or nuclear-space Minlos theorem. Cameron–Martin vectors and typical samples also have different meanings.

Further development

Specify the actual topological vector space and covariance, then prove the continuity/tightness assumptions of the chosen extension theorem.

Revised question

Why is M=Π+R inconsistent with a Perron eigenvalueφ when Πr=r and Rr=0?

The August10 source simultaneously claimed λ≈1.618,Π=rℓᵀ,R=M−Π,Rr=0 and M^k→Π. These assertions cannot all hold. The correct decomposition is elementary and makes the normalization error decisive.

Definitions and assumptions

Let Mr=λr,ℓᵀM=λℓᵀ,ℓᵀr=1 and Π=rℓᵀ. Assume λ is simple and all other eigenvalues have modulus belowλ>0.

Correct spectral projection decomposition

With R=M−λΠ, one has Π²=Π,ΠR=RΠ=0 and M^k=λ^kΠ+R^k for k≥1. Therefore(M/λ)^k→Π whenρ(R)<λ. Defining R=M−Π instead gives Rr=(λ−1)r.

The normalization gives Π²=r(ℓᵀr)ℓᵀ=Π and MΠ=ΠM=λΠ. SubtractingλΠ yields the zero cross-products, so binomial expansion has only the two pure terms. Powers of R/λ tend to zero in finite dimension when its spectral radius is below one, including possible polynomial Jordan factors. The erroneous definition subtracts only r from Mr, leaving(λ−1)r, which directly contradicts the claimed annihilation unlessλ=1. Also a number1−ρ(R) is not a universal transient norm budget for a nonnormal matrix.

Use the symmetric Fibonacci matrix M=[[1,1],[1,0]].

Its eigenvalues areφ and−1/φ. The orthogonal PF projection isΠ=(1/(φ²+1))[[φ²,φ],[φ,1]]. Here R=−φ⁻¹(I−Π), and normalized errors decay exactly asφ^(−2k). Unnormalized M^k grows along r rather than converging.

A single exact eigenvector calculation exposes the historical inconsistency and supplies the corrected convergence theorem.

General nonsymmetric matrices may have large transient constants. Spectral radius alone does not certify a numerical solver or perturbation margin.

Revised question

Which spectral assumptions justify a Chebyshev residual bound, and why is a generic preconditioner label insufficient?

The solver narrative named Chebyshev spectrum shaping without recovered operators. A positive-definite matrix with a known interval admits an exact polynomial bound. The assumptions explain why the same formula cannot be transferred blindly to a nonnormal operator.

Definitions and assumptions

Let A be real symmetric positive definite with spectrum in[a,b],0<a<b. Set c=(a+b)/2,d=(b−a)/2 and p_m(λ)=T_m((c−λ)/d)/T_m(c/d), where T_m(cosθ)=cos(mθ). Then p_m(0)=1.

Uniform residual polynomial bound

For e_m=p_m(A)e₀, ||e_m||₂≤|T_m(c/d)|⁻¹||e₀||₂≤2((√κ−1)/(√κ+1))^m||e₀||₂,κ=b/a.

Derivation or proof

The affine map sends[a,b] to[−1,1], where|T_m|≤1. The spectral theorem turns the matrix norm into the maximum scalar modulus on its spectrum. For z>1, T_m(z)=(w^m+w^(−m))/2 with w=z+√(z²−1)>1, so its reciprocal is at most2w^(−m). At z=c/d, w=(√κ+1)/(√κ−1), giving the formula. A nonsymmetric right preconditioner can destroy symmetry in the Euclidean inner product; eigenvalue placement alone then does not justify the same norm equality. One must identify an appropriate energy inner product or use a different resolvent-based argument.

Worked example

Take A=diag(1,4),m=1.

Here c/d=5/3 and p₁(λ)=1−2λ/5. Its eigenvalue multipliers are3/5 and−3/5, so the exact worst-case contraction is3/5. The general asymptotic bound is looser but valid.

The interval, polynomial normalization and norm are part of the theorem, not implementation details.

Scope

No source preconditioner matrix or spectrum certificate was recovered. This does not validate the historical solver’s claimed performance.

Further development

Construct a symmetric positive preconditioner with certified spectral bounds, then compare finite-step residual norms against the exact polynomial certificate.

The August10 narrative compiler included L-BFGS scaling and Armijo backtracking. A complete quadratic example checks its line search and scale. The inverse-update formula identifies the separate curvature safeguard required for positive-definite search directions.

Definitions and assumptions

Let H be symmetric positive definite,s=x⁺−x,y=∇f(x⁺)−∇f(x),ρ=(yᵀs)⁻¹. The inverse-BFGS update is H⁺=(I−ρsyᵀ)H(I−ρysᵀ)+ρssᵀ.

If yᵀs>0, then H⁺ is positive definite. An Armijo decrease test alone does not guarantee this curvature condition.

For any z≠0, zᵀH⁺z=wᵀHw+ρ(sᵀz)² with w=(I−ρysᵀ)z. Both terms are nonnegative. If sᵀz≠0 the second is positive; if it is zero then w=z and the first is positive. This proves the claim. Armijo bounds f(x+αp) against f(x)+c₁α∇fᵀp, but does not bound the new directional derivative; a curvature/Wolfe condition or an explicit yᵀs safeguard is additional. The scale H₀=(sᵀy)/(yᵀy)I is positive only under the same sign requirement and a nonzero denominator.

Use f=(x₀−1)²+(x₁+2)² at x=(4,−6).

The test checks real derivative and update identities rather than merely a solver status.

No global L-BFGS convergence theorem follows from one quadratic. Nonsmooth objectives and skipped or damped updates require their own hypotheses.

Revised question

What exact map preserves a first-cohomology obstruction, and why are cover-preserving labels alone insufficient?

The August12–13 assistant asserted literal equivalence across four domains. A finite cochain complex gives a valid obstruction test, while an explicit counterexample shows why arbitrary adapters do not induce isomorphisms. The historical random surrogate matrices are not adopted as geometric data.

Definitions and assumptions

A cochain complex has C⁰→δ⁰ C¹→δ¹ C² with δ¹δ⁰=0. Its H¹ is kerδ¹/imδ⁰. A cochain map F satisfies Fδ=δF. A cochain homotopy equivalence has an inverse up to maps of the form δh+hδ.

Homotopy equivalence preserves obstruction classes

A cochain homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism on H¹. An arbitrary cochain map, even between three-patch constructions, need not be injective or surjective.

Derivation or proof

A cochain map sends cocycles to cocycles and coboundaries to coboundaries, hence induces cohomology maps. If GF−I=δh+hδ, then on a cocycle z the difference GFz−z=δhz is a coboundary. Thus the induced composite is the identity; the other homotopy proves the inverse composite. Without these hypotheses the zero map between identical nontrivial complexes is already a counterexample to injectivity. Cover preservation and finite-limit preservation by themselves are not a substitute for the specific descent and comparison hypotheses of a sheaf-cohomology theorem.

Worked example

Use the triangle graph complex C⁰=Q³,C¹=Q³,C²=0 with oriented edge differences.

The vertex-to-edge matrix has rank two, so H¹ has dimension one. The constant1 edge circulation is a nonzero class. The identity preserves it and the zero chain map kills it. Filling the triangle adds a rank-one δ¹ condition and removes this class entirely.

The domain adapters need actual complexes, restriction maps and a proved comparison, not shared names for a nonzero number.
